itinerary.cal: Climbed roughly July-September once approach gullies and Terror Basin snowfields have melted out; a North Cascades National Park wilderness permit (reservable in advance, or first-come at Marblemount) is required for the Terror Basin camp.

days.note: A steep, sweaty climb out of the Goodell Creek trailhead through forest and heather slopes into Terror Basin, gaining nearly 6,000 ft to the flat camping shelf at roughly 5,800 ft below the Southern Pickets crest. Parties carry a full multi-day rack, rope, and several days of food, since the route is entirely off-trail once past the first mile or two.
days.title: Approach to Terror Basin

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Goodell Creek TH, permit and rack in hand

schedule.label: Clear treeline
schedule.detail: Onto open heather and talus below the basin

schedule.label: Reach Terror Basin camp
schedule.detail: Flat gravel bench at ~5,800 ft with water and views of the crest

days.objective: Reach the Terror Basin high camp

days.note: An alpine-start day climbing from camp to the Terror-Rake col, then following the crest on mixed 4th/5th-class terrain (to roughly 5.9) to the summit at 7,869 ft. The descent reverses the ridge with a series of rappels back to the col and down to camp, so the rope stays on for most of the day.
days.title: Climb The Rake, ridge traverse route

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start with rack, single rope, and minimal water/food

schedule.label: Gain the Terror-Rake col
schedule.detail: Steep gully/snow finger to the notch

schedule.label: Start ridge pitches
schedule.detail: Mixed climbing along the crest, up to 5.9 in spots

schedule.label: Begin rappel descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge with a series of raps back toward the col

days.objective: Summit The Rake and return to Terror Basin camp

days.note: Break camp and descend the approach route in reverse — steep heather and forest back down to the highway. Knees take the brunt of it; most parties are back at the car by mid-afternoon.
days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to Goodell Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip: one day backpacking into Terror Basin camp, a long technical day climbing The Rake's ridge crest and rappelling back to camp, and a day hiking out — roughly 16 miles and ~7,700 ft of gain round trip.

access.fees: $10 per person backcountry recreation fee plus a $6 nonrefundable permit/reservation fee — applies to advance Recreation.gov reservations, early-access lottery entries, and walk-up permits alike; no charge for youth 15 and under. This per-person structure replaced the former flat ~$20–26 per-permit fee in March 2024.
access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Reserved permits must be picked up by 11am on the trip's start date or the reservation is cancelled; camp only within your assigned cross-country zone.
access.permit: NPS backcountry permit required for any overnight stay ($10/person/night + $6 nonrefundable fee as of March 2024 — no longer free). Reservable in advance via Recreation.gov, or obtained as a walk-up (about 40% of capacity is held for walk-ups) at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount, (360) 854-7245 / noca_wilderness@nps.gov.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high — the Crescent Creek approach into the Southern Pickets involves sustained off-trail bushwhacking, steep brush/talus, and significant elevation gain typical of Pickets approaches; expect a full, grueling approach day(s) before any climbing begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Heavy multi-day alpine/overnight kit (bivy or camp gear, rack, glacier/snow travel gear for the approach in early season) — expect 35-50+ lb packs for the approach

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-day approach typical (1-2 days in via Crescent Creek basin) given the remoteness and difficulty of the approach; not a single-push objective for most parties

route-finding on loose, exposed, unmarked alpine ridge terrain
self-rescue and remote wilderness first-response competence
off-trail navigation and bushwhack approach experience
snow/glacier travel basics for early-season approach conditions
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced alpine climbers only — comfortable with remote, unrescuable terrain, route-finding on a serrated alpine ridge, and multi-day self-sufficiency; prior North Cascades or similarly committing range experience strongly recommended

itinerary.cal: North Cascades NP wilderness permit required for camping in Terror/Crescent Creek Basin; best conditions are typically late July–September once snow on the Barrier and the Eye Col approach gullies has receded.

days.note: A long, hard approach day: from the Goodell Creek Cross-Country trailhead, follow the old roadbed and boot path up through Terror Creek drainage, over The Barrier (steep class 2-3 scrambling), and across Crescent Creek Basin to a flat camp spot with water below Mount Terror at ~6,050 ft. Most parties go straight to this camp in one day rather than splitting it with a separate Terror Basin camp.
days.title: Approach to Crescent Creek Camp

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Goodell Creek Cross-Country Zone Access trailhead.

schedule.label: Terror Creek crossing and old roadbed
schedule.detail: Roadbed for ~4 miles, then steep boot path from ~1,700 ft up through treeline.

schedule.label: Cross The Barrier
schedule.detail: Serious class 2-3 ridge crossing; the technical crux of the approach.

schedule.label: Traverse Crescent Creek Basin
schedule.detail: Stay near 5,800 ft, traverse about a mile to camp.

schedule.label: Make camp
schedule.detail: Flat site with water below Mount Terror, ~6,050 ft.

days.objective: Reach climbing camp below Mount Terror / West Twin Needle

days.note: A full technical day from camp: descend to the head of Crescent Creek, traverse below the Eye Col gully, then climb chockstone-filled terrain into class 5 ground and the East Face 5.7 Direct to the summit. Descend via two 60m rappels through the Himmelhorn-West Twin notch back toward camp, aiming to be off the rock before dark.
days.title: Summit push via South Route / East Face 5.7 Direct

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Early alpine start; helmet, rack, and 2x60m rope.

schedule.label: Drop to Crescent Creek headwaters
schedule.detail: Descend roughly 300 ft from camp before the rising traverse.

schedule.label: Traverse below Eye Col
schedule.detail: Rising traverse past the adjacent buttress toward the south gully.

schedule.label: Enter south gully / chockstones
schedule.detail: Scramble and short pitches through chockstone terrain into class 5 ground.

schedule.label: East Face 5.7 Direct
schedule.detail: Roped pitches to the summit ridge.

schedule.label: Summit, then rappel descent
schedule.detail: Two 60m raps through the Himmelhorn-West Twin notch, then reverse the approach to camp by evening.

days.objective: Climb West Twin Needle and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the approach: back across Crescent Creek Basin, over The Barrier, down through the Terror Creek drainage and old roadbed to the trailhead. Water can be scarce on this leg in late summer, so plan refill stops.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, car-to-car trip of roughly 19.5 miles RT with about 7,900 ft of net elevation range; one long approach day in, one full technical summit day, one long day out.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Very high - multi-day, largely trail-less approach with sustained elevation gain/loss and off-trail navigation to reach Crescent Creek basin before any technical climbing begins
fitnessSpec.packWeight: 50-65 lbs typical for a self-supported multi-day expedition (bivy gear, technical rack, food/fuel for several days)

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 2-3 days of trail-less approach through the Southern Pickets (e.g., via Terror Basin/Crescent Creek) before reaching the base of the route
requiredSkills: Comfortable leading 5.7 alpine rock on loose, unfamiliar rock (Grade III commitment)
Off-trail route-finding and bushwhacking through trail-less basins
Basic glacier/snow travel skills for approach terrain near Crescent Creek
Self-rescue and remote wilderness first aid competency given the isolation
Multi-pitch anchor building, rappelling, and efficient party movement
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced alpine climbers only, with prior multi-day expedition experience in the North Cascades - this is a committing, remote objective with scarce route beta

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
waypoints.note: Unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek; NW Forest Pass and a self-issue wilderness permit (or WIC permit in Marblemount) required.
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is an unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, along with a self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead, or one from the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount if you plan to camp in the Terror or Crescent Creek basins.

waypoints.name: Upper trail fork
waypoints.note: Maintained forestry-road-bed trail ends here; climbers' path continues with diminishing cairns/flagging toward Terror Creek.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Ford Terror Creek at a shallow braid; crossing depth is very flow-dependent and can be a wade in high water.

waypoints.name: The Barrier
waypoints.note: Steep, brushy, loose ridge (spur off Mt. Degenhardt) separating Terror Creek and Crescent Creek basins; cross via a loose ledge system near the lower Terror Glacier or a higher moat crossing below Degenhardt — classic sustained 'Pickets Class 3' that turns parties back.

waypoints.name: Crescent Creek Basin camp (below Mt. Terror)
waypoints.note: Established high camp on a flat bench below Mount Terror with meltwater from two overhead slab streams; the basin runs 6,050–6,440 ft.

waypoints.name: Eye Col gully traverse
waypoints.note: Drop ~300 ft below the moraine to Crescent Creek's head, then rising-traverse below the Eye Col gully past an adjacent buttress on a minor rib to a notch, avoiding a closed chimney and loose choss.

waypoints.name: West Twin Needle
waypoints.note: Final class 5.7 pitch through larger chockstones/a narrow crack above the col, then class 2-3 scrambling under white slabs to the true summit; descend via rappels off the Himmelhorn–West Twin Needle col.

before.detailed_rack: A light alpine rock rack (small-to-mid cams and nuts) covers the low-5th-class pitches and 5.7 crux; carry a few extra slings/quickdraws for the chockstone-choked gully sections and glacier travel gear (axe, and crampons if snow lingers) for the Crescent Creek Basin / Mustard Glacier approach depending on season.
before.overview: West Twin Needle (7,936 ft) is the taller, western spire of the Twin Needles, a pair of rock pinnacles in the Southern Pickets immediately west of Mount Terror. Its slightly lower twin to the east (about 7,840+ ft) is the more technically serious of the pair; West Twin Needle carries easier class 3-4 flanks but this South Route tackles steeper 5.7 rock directly up its south/east side above Crescent Creek Basin. First climbed August 17, 1932 by William Degenhardt, James Martin, and Herb Strandberg, it sees very few ascents each year owing to the multi-day cross-country approach required to reach it.
